chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who has two colors of the same type of food, and their prices are different, and one is better than the other, so he mixes them all together and then sells them at a single price. He said: 'It is not suitable for him to do that, for he is deceiving the Muslims, until he makes it clear (to the buyer).'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on mixing different qualities of food and selling them at a single price?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the prohibition of *ghish* (deception) in commercial transactions, specifically when a seller blends high and low-quality goods of the same type to sell at a uniform price without disclosure. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on transparency and fairness (*adl*) in trade, ensuring that the buyer is not misled about the true value of the commodity. It serves as a practical application of the broader Islamic ethical mandate to avoid hidden defects in sales.
